# Meerschaum Documentation

> Incremental data pipelines in SQL and Python.

## Home
- [Home](https://meerschaum.io/): Meerschaum turns queries and Python functions into named data streams called Pipes. Register a source, sync it, and query the results from your database, Python, or the web console.

## Get Started
- [Install and set up](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/): Your first Pipe needs Python and a few local rows. No database server or Docker setup is required.
- [Your first Pipe](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/bootstrap/): A Pipe connects a data source to a table you can keep up to date. Let's collect temperature readings in a local SQLite database.
- [Sync new rows](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/incremental-sync/): Your first Pipe already has one reading. Add another to its source:
- [Your first Pipeline](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/pipelines/): One Pipe collects readings. Another converts them. A Pipeline runs those steps in the right order and gives the workflow a name.
- [Explore the console](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/start-api/): See the same Pipes and Pipeline from your browser. Continue in the workspace from Your first Pipeline.
- [Save a project](https://meerschaum.io/get-started/compose-projects/): A Compose project keeps your Pipes, connectors, and plugins in one folder. Put it in version control and run the same workflow again.

## Reference
- [Reference](https://meerschaum.io/reference/): Find commands, settings, and operational guides for an existing Meerschaum installation.
- [🚰 Pipes](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/): A Meerschaum pipe represents a data stream into a table and the necessary parameters to sync new data.
- [🥾 Bootstrapping](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/bootstrapping/): The bootstrap pipes action includes a setup wizard to guide you through the process of creating new pipes. In this tutorial, we'll be looking at the prompts you'll encounter to help you better underst
- [📥 Syncing](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/syncing/): I wrote my master's thesis on comparing syncing strategies.
- [📖 Reading Data](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/reading/): Use Pipe.getdata() and its convenience wrappers to read rows from the instance.
- [🔖 Tags](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/tags/): You can define custom groupings of pipes with tags. Consider the example below:
- [🧩 Parameters](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/parameters/): This page catalogs useful keys in the parameters dictionary.
- [🔤 Data Types](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/dtypes/): This page explains what Meerschaum data types (dtypes) are, when to use each one, and how dtype coercion behaves during syncs. For the dtype table in context with the rest of the metadata, see paramet
- [🧹 Maintenance](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/maintenance/): Over time a pipe's target table accumulates dead rows, stale planner statistics, and uncompressed history. Meerschaum provides a family of maintenance actions to keep tables lean and queries fast. Eac
- [🔒 Access and Locks](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipes/access-and-locks/): Meerschaum is open by default—every user sees and edits every pipe within their permissions until you configure access or locks. Two reserved parameters control who owns a pipe and what can happen to
- [🕸️ Pipelines](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/): > New in v5. The Syncing Engine tracks pipe dependencies, computes the exact window each node needs, runs independent branches in parallel, and records every run.
- [🎼 Compose Definitions](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/compose/): Declare what runs in pipelines:. Use jobs: to decide when it runs.
- [🗃️ Engine State](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/state/): The Syncing Engine creates no local database files. All state lives on your instance as internal mrsm tables—in mrsminternal on PostgreSQL and MSSQL (suffixed for non-default schemas so instances shar
- [♾️ Continuous Mode](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/continuous/): Keep pipes syncing continuously with --loop (polling on an interval) or --listen (push-based streaming sources like MQTT, Kafka, AMQP, or webhooks).
- [📊 Visualization](https://meerschaum.io/reference/pipelines/visualization/): One typed event stream drives the terminal live view, Gantt timelines, web console, Python callbacks, and HTTP SSE:
- [🔌 Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/): Meerschaum coordinates everything via connectors. Use cases for Connectors include fetching and inserting data when syncing pipes.
- [🗂️ SQL Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/sql-connectors/): Meerschaum's first-class connector is the SQLConnector. Several built-in sql connectors are defined by default:
- [🗄️ Instance Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/instance-connectors/): Instance connectors store pipes' metadata (and may also be used as a source connector, e.g. the #!python SQLConnector).
- [🗝️ Valkey Connectors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/valkey/): The ValkeyConnector syncs pipes to a Valkey instance. Valkey is an in-memory key-value store forked from Redis, so the same connector also works against a Redis server.
- [❓ Other Connector Types](https://meerschaum.io/reference/connectors/other-connectors/): Though the SQL Connector is the premier Meerschaum connector type, there are plenty of other implementations of the instance connector interface.
- [🥞 Meerschaum Stack](https://meerschaum.io/reference/stack/): The Stack uses Docker Compose to run TimescaleDB, the Meerschaum API and web console, Valkey, and Grafana together. Start it with mrsm stack up -d.
- [Upgrades and backups](https://meerschaum.io/reference/stack/upgrades/): Pulling newer images (mrsm stack pull or mrsm upgrade mrsm) updates your containers, not the database extensions or PostgreSQL format inside your volume. Use these four guided commands to maintain you
- [🌐 API Instance](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/): The Meerschaum API instance (and Web Console) lets you manage pipes, jobs, and connectors over the Internet. Start the API server with the stack or via start api; see Deployment below for ways to run
- [Security and Tokens](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/tokens/): Meerschaum tokens are long-lived API keys that grant programmatic access to a Meerschaum instance. They are a secure way to authenticate for services like IoT devices or CI/CD pipelines without using
- [Permissions and Rate Limits](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/permissions/): Control who can reach your API server and what they can run under api:permissions (mrsm edit config api):
- [Teams on One Instance](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/teams/): Multiple teams can share one Meerschaum API instance—using the same web console, HTTP API, and MCP server—while seeing only their own pipes, jobs, connectors, and plugins. An isolated team is walled o
- [Team Execution Environments](https://meerschaum.io/reference/team-executors/): Run an isolated team's jobs, plugins, virtual environments, and web terminals in its own container or remote executor while the main API keeps ownership of login, permissions, and routing.
- [Pipelines, Access and Actions over HTTP](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/routes/): In addition to core pipe, user, token, plugin, and job routes, the API server exposes endpoints for saved Pipelines, engine runs, teams and pipe access, and background actions. Browse the live OpenAPI
- [NGINX](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/nginx/): Hosting Meerschaum behind NGINX is a great way set up TLS/SSL with Let's Encrypt (certbot), especially when several sites share port 443. (The API server can also serve HTTPS by itself: see TLS / SSL
- [Web Console](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/web-console/): The Web Console is a graphical UI for your API instance. Start the server and open http://localhost:8000:
- [Sync Metrics](https://meerschaum.io/reference/api-instance/sync-metrics/): Find slow or failing syncs, and see how much data each Pipe or Pipeline changes.
- [🤖 MCP Server](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/): Meerschaum ships a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI agent can discover your pipes, read their data, and run actions without you writing any glue code.
- [Tool Reference](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/tools/): Every tool, resource, and prompt the MCP server exposes, generated
- [Security](https://meerschaum.io/reference/mcp/security/): The MCP server hands an AI agent the same capabilities a person has at the CLI or web console. Treat a token for it exactly as you would a Meerschaum login.
- [🎼 Compose](https://meerschaum.io/reference/compose/): Meerschaum Compose does the same for Meerschaum as Docker Compose does for Docker: you can consolidate everything into a single YAML file, including all of the pipes and configuration needed for your
- [⏯️ Actions](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/): Run mrsm help (or mrsm -h) for every action and its options. Add -h to any command (mrsm sync pipes -h) or run mrsm help sync pipes for action details.
- [📺 Watch and Shell Shortcuts](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/watch/): show prints something once; watch keeps it on screen as it changes. watch run and watch jobs are full-screen views (new in v5) that take the whole terminal and give it back as it was when you leave; w
- [👥 Teams, Access and Locks](https://meerschaum.io/reference/actions/teams-and-access/): Meerschaum is open by default: on an instance where nobody sets up teams, access or locks, every
- [Background Jobs](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/): Add -d to run an action in the background. Give it a name so you can find its logs later:
- [Schedules](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/schedules/): Use --schedule (-s) to repeat an action. Add -d to keep it running in the background:
- [Executors](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/executors/): An executor runs a job. Select one with -e (--executor-keys):
- [Access](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/access/): API-created jobs record the authenticated owner and that user's primary team. Requests cannot assign a different owner or team. Jobs created on the host through the CLI, Compose, systemd, or Python be
- [Automatic Runs](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/runs/): Clicking Sync on a Pipe or Run on a Pipeline starts a temporary worker. The console lists it under Runs, keeping one-off work out of persistent Jobs. A manually created one-shot Job stays in Jobs.
- [Health](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/health/): Repeating jobs record each completed run, called a lap. mrsm show jobs and the console show the last successful sync and whether work is failing or stalled.
- [Startup stagger](https://meerschaum.io/reference/background-jobs/startup/): Starting many jobs together can overload a host. Meerschaum spreads bulk starts with random delay, host load checks, and a per-root limit on starting workers.
- [🔧 Data Analysis Tools](https://meerschaum.io/reference/data-analysis-tools/): Meerschaum comes with a pre-configured data visualization stack so that you can spend your time on analysis rather than configuring servers.
- [➕ Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/): Meerschaum plugins let you ingest any data source into pipes as well as defining custom actions, connectors, API endpoints, dash apps, and more.
- [✍️ Writing Your Own](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/writing-plugins/): Rust plugins can be a single .rs file for actions, data sources, or connectors. See the Rust quickstart to get started, or the advanced guide for packaging and the full SDK. The examples below use Pyt
- [🤔 Types of Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/types-of-plugins/): > This page introduces the different types of Meerschaum plugins. For technical information, consult the Writing Your Own Plugins tutorial.
- [🖥️ Web Pages and Routes](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/web-pages/): Plugins add pages to the Web Console with #!python @webpage, make them interactive with Dash callbacks, and add API routes with #!python @apiplugin. This page covers who may use them (signed-in visito
- [🗃️ Caching](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/caching/): Some things are slow to compute: a query over a big table, a chart, a call to someone else's API. meerschaum.utils.cache remembers the result for a while, shares it with every process of your deployme
- [🧪 Testing Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/testing/): meerschaum.testing is a pytest plugin: your tests get a throwaway Meerschaum root, a fresh SQLite instance for each test, pipes that clean up after themselves, the web API in the test process and the

- [🚀 Repositories](https://meerschaum.io/reference/plugins/repositories/): Meerschaum gives you the ability to easily install and create plugins. Refer to the guide below on how to install, write, and publish plugins.
- [🌳 Environment Variables](https://meerschaum.io/reference/environment/): Manage Meerschaum's paths, configuration, and runtime behavior with environment variables. Run mrsm show environment to list active MRSM variables, or mrsm show config to inspect the resolved configur
- [🩺 Troubleshooting](https://meerschaum.io/reference/troubleshooting/): A symptom-driven guide to common Meerschaum issues (Symptom → Cause → Fix). For terminology, see the glossary.
- [🤔 FAQ](https://meerschaum.io/faq/): Below is a list of common questions and issues you may encounter. If you have suggestions, please join the FAQ Suggestions discussion on the GitHub repository!

## Tutorials
- [Learn by building](https://meerschaum.io/tutorials/): Start small, then add one idea at a time. The beginner path uses local SQLite data and works without an external API or database server.

## Docs
- [Developer docs](https://meerschaum.io/docs/): Use Meerschaum in an application, provide data from a plugin, or add a command.
- [Python](https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/): Install the package, then import the SDK:
- [Pipes](https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/pipes/): A Pipe stores a named data stream on an instance. This example uses the built-in local SQLite instance and supplies its own rows:
- [Pipelines](https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/pipelines/): A Pipeline selects Pipes and runs their dependencies in order. Once your Pipes are registered, save a workflow on their instance:
- [Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/plugins/): Save readings.py in your plugins directory, or use mrsm bootstrap plugins readings to create it:
- [Rust](https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/): Embed Pipes and the engine in a Rust application, or extend an installed Meerschaum with a native plugin.
- [Embedding](https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/embedding/): Library applications disable default features to avoid building the full CLI:
- [Pipes](https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/pipes/): This local example provides rows directly and writes them through the SQL connector. Use the dependencies from Embedding.
- [Pipelines](https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/pipelines/): The engine takes a connector registry, a home instance, and run options. Its selection chooses targets and how far to traverse their dependencies.
- [Plugins](https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/plugins/): A single-file plugin needs no Cargo project. Save greetings.rs in your plugins directory:

## Changelog
- [Changelog](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/): Meerschaum 5 brings a Rust core, dependency-aware Pipelines, and a new web console.
- [v5](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v5/): Maintenance release: leaner Docker images that share layers, stricter non-admin SQL checks, faster API reads on large SQL instances, and console, web terminal, and sync fixes.
- [v4](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v4/): Historical release notes for the 4.x series.
- [v3](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v3/): Historical release notes for the 3.x series.
- [v2](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v2/): Historical release notes for the 2.x series.
- [v1](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v1/): Historical release notes for the 1.x series.
- [v0](https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v0/): Historical release notes for the 0.x series.
